newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE UP IN TIGHT MARKET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES EDGE UP IN TIGHT MARKET.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market edged up on Friday as liquidity tightened due to a lack of treasury bill maturities.
"The market is a bit tight today and we opened with a shortage of Z$63.1 million and as a result rates are a bit tight," one dealer said.
The dealer said there was no daily tender on Friday, but added that Z$55 million worth of treasury bills at the weekly Thursday tender yielded an average rate of 16.64 percent.
They said discount houses were selling the central bank paper on the secondary market at 16.50 percent, slightly lower from Thursday's 16.60 percent
Call money ranged in a 17 to 17.25 percent band, up from 16 percent while bank bills were at 17.75 percent (buying) from 16.65 percent and 17.25 percent (selling) versus 16.60 percent.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought and sold at 18 percent and 17.50 percent respectively from 17 and 16.75 percent.
